recognition: HMRC letter about Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: telling a sole trader or landlord they need to use MTD (customer awareness letter), or about paying under MTD (payment awareness letter), or reminders about quarterly updates.

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax means sole traders and landlords keep digital records in MTD-compatible software and send HMRC quarterly updates, then a final declaration after the tax year, instead of only one Self Assessment return.
facts_for_explanation.who_and_when: Qualifying income (self-employment plus property income) over £50,000 in 2024-25: from 6 April 2026 (sign-up is still open). Over £30,000 in 2025-26: from 6 April 2027. Over £20,000 in 2026-27: from 6 April 2028. HMRC writes to people who must start.
facts_for_explanation.sign_up: You must be registered for Self Assessment and have filed a return in the last two years. Some people are exempt, for example if they are digitally excluded – they must still file a Self Assessment return.
facts_for_explanation.payment_letter: A payment awareness letter is about paying the tax: the amounts are still paid by the Self Assessment payment dates (31 January and 31 July).
